title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
abstract: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.
summary: This work proposes using the phase of a Bargmann invariant in matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity witness. The phase isolates a commutator term that is predicted to be non-zero by quantum theory but must vanish in any classical or semiclassical model. This offers a pathway to test quantum gravity effects using current or near-future interferometry techniques.
main_problem: To identify a quantum gravity signature in matter-wave interferometry that cannot be explained by classical or branchwise-definite gravitational field models.
main_result: The Bargmann invariant phase, which isolates the graviton commutator term, provides a quantum signature that must be non-zero if quantum gravity effects are present, as it vanishes in all classically simulable models.
method: The analysis uses the coherence factor of matter-wave interferometers coupled to linearized gravity, comparing the full quantum result against semiclassical approximations.
model_or_system: The system involves matter-wave interferometers with sources in spatial superposition, coupled linearly to linearized gravity. The evolution is analyzed via the matter coherence factor, which is decomposed into conservative, fluctuation, and commutator phases.

important_parameters: The commutator term $(X|GPJ|Y)$, which is independent of the graviton state and Newtonian interactions.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes sources are additive and relies on the comparison between the full quantum evolution and models restricted to branchwise-definite dynamics.

paper_structure: The paper develops the coherence factorization, derives the commutator term via the Bargmann invariant, establishes the quantumness budget inequality, and compares the quantum prediction against classical limits.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, measurable, and theoretically robust observable ($B$) derived from fundamental quantum principles (commutators) to test quantum gravity effects using an interferometric platform, linking quantum field theory to experimental signatures.
